ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identity verification under FINTRAC guidance and the PCMLTFA; mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders above 25%, and individuals with significant control against UN Security Council sanctions, Global Affairs Canada consolidated Canadian sanctions list, domestic and foreign PEP databases, and OFAC SDN list as a secondary standard. Adverse-media checks and ongoing UBO monitoring are required. Because Paddle and Lemon Squeezy operate as merchant-of-record payment facilitators, confirm the selected PSP has independent KYC/AML coverage; however, founder-level PEP and sanctions screening remains the legal agent's responsibility throughout the corporate lifecycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names may be in English, French, or both official languages. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must include a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Incorporated, Corporation, Limited, Ltée, Limitée, or Société par actions de régime fédéral. Distinctiveness is assessed in both official languages under the Canada Business Corporations Act, and a NUANS search is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A federal NUANS name reservation is valid for 90 days and is not normally renewable; after expiry, a fresh NUANS request and fee must be filed. If Corporations Canada rejects a proposed name, the incorporator may file a reconsideration request in writing to the Director, Corporate Governance Directorate, Corporations Canada, within 30 days of the rejection notice, setting out grounds for distinctiveness and non-confusion. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, judicial review may be sought in the Federal Court under the Federal Courts Act; alternatively, a revised name may be resubmitted with a new NUANS search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if the virtual office supplies a physical street address in the province of registration, is not a post-office box, and is staffed to accept service of process during ordinary business hours. A purely remote or telephone-only virtual address is not compliant for a federal corporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximately 5% per annum in the absence of red flags or regulatory triggers. Corporations Canada does not conduct routine unannounced premises inspections, but Canada Revenue Agency, FINTRAC, or provincial tax authorities may perform warrant-based or compliance inspections if the corporation becomes subject to audit, AML obligations, or material tax indicia.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended — Part IA (ss. 5-14: incorporation and articles of incorporation), ss. 19-20 (registered office and corporate records), Part V (ss. 101-121: directors and officers); implementing regulations SOR/2001-512.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), Government of Canada — Online Filing Centre
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 4001 — Articles of Incorporation, together with Form 4003 (Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors) and Form 4006 (Consent to Act as Director), filed electronically under the CBCA Regulations, SOR/2001-512
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the CBCA. A federal business corporation may be incorporated with nil or nominal stated capital; shares are issued for such consideration as the directors determine under CBCA s. 25. No escrow account requirement applies to a private non-reporting micro-SaaS issuer; escrow rules are limited to prescribed securities transactions and prospectus offerings.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscription of its founding shareholder and issues the initial allotment of common shares in consideration of nominal cash and contributed intellectual property, as recorded in the securities register. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address specified in Form 4003 and that corporate records be maintained there. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, each to hold office at the pleasure of the Board. RESOLVED, that the Board adopt the general corporate by-law and authorize execution of banking resolutions and ancillary filings to give full force to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (ISED) via the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system, accessible through Corporations Canada's online portal or accredited service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the mandatory legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or 'Incorporated'), conduct a NUANS report for the proposed English and French name forms, and review the results for confusing similarity with existing federal corporations, provincial entities, and registered trademarks under the Trade-marks Act. If the SaaS product brand is the operative trade name, either adopt a distinct corporate name or incorporate as a numbered company, reserving the brand as a separate trademark registration administered by the Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO).
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in English and/or French
NUANS name search request and report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report flags a confusingly similar name, select an alternative distinctive keyword and obtain a fresh NUANS report, or proceed as a numbered company; an administrative objection may be filed with CIPO within the statutory response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (ISED) — legal review conducted by the incorporating practitioner or online filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 4001 setting out the corporate name or numbered company designation, the province of the registered office, the class and maximum number of shares (e.g., unlimited common voting shares and optionally preferred shares), any restrictions on share transfers, the number of first directors, and any permitted business restrictions relevant to the software scope (ISIC 6201). Complete Form 4006 (Consent to Act as Director) for each Canada-resident director and Form 4003 (Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors). Verify compliance with CBCA ss. 5-6 and confirm that no business restriction conflicts with the Micro-SaaS subscription model.
required_dossiers: Form 4006 — Consent to Act as Director for each first director
Form 4003 — Initial Registered Office Address and First Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada issues a notice of defect or query, the filer must amend the flagged articles, obtain corrected director consents, and resubmit within the prescribed response period; the originally submitted filing fee remains credited toward the corrected submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a Corporations Canada online account, complete the electronic articles questionnaire mirroring Form 4001, upload the NUANS report and director consents, and remit the CAD 200 incorporation fee by credit card. Upon validation of the name and statutory elements, the system issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation, which becomes the conclusive evidence of corporate existence under CBCA s. 256.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected, the filer receives an electronic correction notice specifying the deficiency; correct the flagged items and resubmit within the stated deadline. If the name is refused at this stage, submit revised articles with a new NUANS-based name or a numbered company designation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance Board and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada; corporate records registered at the registered office under CBCA s. 20
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Promptly after the Certificate of Incorporation, hold the first organizational board meeting or execute unanimous consent resolutions under CBCA s. 117: adopt By-law No. 1 governing general business and financial matters, ratify the allotment and issue of shares, elect officers, appoint banking signatories, and approve the opening of corporate bank accounts. Establish the statutory records location at the registered office and record all share subscriptions, director consents, and charter documents.
required_dossiers: By-law No. 1 and organizational resolutions in lieu of meeting
Share subscription agreements and share certificates
Directors' written consents and officer appointment records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum or voting validity is challenged, obtain signed unanimous resolutions in lieu of meeting under CBCA s. 117 and, where a director vacates office, file Form 4005 (Notice of Directors) with Corporations Canada to align the statutory record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Tax and Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO), Federal jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for the 9-digit Business Number and the Corporate Income Tax account within 30 days of incorporation. Open the GST/HST account once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or rolling four-quarter period, noting applicable zero-rated or reverse-charge treatment for digital supplies to non-resident customers. Register separately for the Payroll Deduction account only when employees are hired, and complete any provincial tax information returns coordinated through the federal registration.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and directors' particulars
Estimated annual revenue for GST/HST threshold assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, file Form RC265 (Business Number amendment/withdrawal request) and submit the Certificate of Incorporation and corrected corporate data; GST/HST registration, where applicable, may be backdated to the effective incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Extra-Provincial Registration and Municipal Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial/territorial corporate registry (e.g., ServiceOntario in Ontario, Registry Services in British Columbia, Companies Office in Manitoba) and the relevant municipal business licensing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the province of primary business activities (the SaaS operator's head office or principal administrative location). If the physical presence is outside the province named as the registered office and exceeds the provincial exemption thresholds, file for extra-provincial registration under the applicable provincial Business Corporations Act equivalents. For a purely virtual micro-SaaS with no leased premises, confirm that no municipal trade licence or landlord occupancy permit is triggered; if a co-working or residential home office is used, ensure zoning bylaws permit digital service activities.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registered Office confirming head office location
Lease or co-working agreement only if required by the municipal registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the provincial registry challenges the federal name or certificate, obtain a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation from Corporations Canada, file an application for extra-provincial registration with the provincial registrar, and, where necessary, adopt a supplementary provincial registration name under the provincial extra-provincial registration rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — ISIC 6201 (computer programming and software publishing) micro-SaaS operations involve no physical industrial or manufacturing facility; no federal or provincial industrial operating board imposes a licensing mandate on this digital business scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Required — Lightweight productivity cloud software subscription operations are not a designated trade under provincial licensing frameworks; no manufacturing, production, or operational permit is required at the federal or provincial level for a purely digital distribution model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and, for designated projects, the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada; provincial environmental agencies (e.g., Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks) apply only to physical premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — No physical works, no land disturbance, and no designated project under the Impact Assessment Act (S.C. 2019, c. 28) apply to a virtual cloud-software operator with no owned industrial facility; EIA triggered only if the corporation later establishes a data center, warehouse, or physical processing site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — the micro-SaaS model produces no wastewater, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), or hazardous waste streams. Vigilance standards include compliance with provincial electronic waste stewardship obligations for discarded IT hardware and a procurement preference for third-party cloud providers (e.g., AWS Lightsail, Azure, or regional Canadian hosting) that maintain ISO 14001 or equivalent environmental management certifications.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a home-office or co-working-space SaaS operator with no dedicated industrial facility. If a commercial office lease is executed, the landlord must provide a fire safety certification in compliance with the National Fire Code (NFC) and the applicable provincial fire marshal inspection regime, together with the building's structural load clearance under the National Building Code (NBC). Once the first employee is engaged, register with the relevant provincial workers' compensation authority (e.g., WSIB in Ontario, WorkSafeBC in British Columbia) and obtain an occupational health and safety clearance where the provincial act requires it.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; taxpayer portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO) at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For foreign entities: (1) Determine Canadian nexus — 'carrying on business in Canada' or making taxable supplies of digital products/services to Canadian consumers; (2) if threshold met or commercial activity established, register for a Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) using Form RC1/RC1A, requesting the RT (GST/HST) program account; (3) use the simplified CRA registration channel for non-resident suppliers of digital products/services when there is no physical presence in Canada; (4) CRA issues a 9-digit BN with a 2-letter program-account suffix (e.g., RT0001); (5) a foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada must also file T2 corporate income tax returns and may need provincial/territorial extra-provincial registration; provide certified foreign incorporation documents and director identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian federal business corporation is a per se corporation under the Income Tax Act (ITA), taxed at entity level; CCPC or non-CCPC status determines SBD eligibility; resident corporations taxed on worldwide income; no pass-through or partnership-style transparency; CRA applies its own administrative entity classification for foreign entities (no check-the-box election).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists. Available elections: (i) ITA s.256(9) deemed-Canadian-controlled-private-corporation (CCPC) election; (ii) ITA s.216(1) election for non-residents with Canadian rental income to file on net basis; (iii) ITA s.111(5.1)/(5.2) acquisition-of-control loss-restriction elections; (iv) GST/HST annual versus quarterly filing elections; (v) ETA deemed-supplier elections under the digital-platform rules. Hybrid-mismatch rules under ITA (BEPS Action 2) may override contractual or foreign-entity characterizations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) — federal VAT administered by CRA; 5% GST applies in all provinces; HST at 13% (Ontario) or 15% (NB, NL, NS, PEI); Quebec imposes separate QST administered by Revenu Québec; BC/SK/MB impose separate provincial sales taxes outside CRA administration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small-supplier threshold under ETA s.148(2) based on taxable supplies in the current calendar quarter and the preceding four calendar quarters (worldwide taxable revenues); for non-resident suppliers of digital products/digital services to Canadian consumers, the same CAD 30,000 threshold over a 12-month period triggers mandatory simplified GST/HST registration; no threshold for persons engaged in a commercial activity considered 'carrying on business in Canada' if persistent and substantial.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — CRA does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or fiscal-API integration. Electronic invoices are valid if they contain the prescribed ETA s.3 information (supplier name/BN, recipient, date, taxable amount, tax rate, tax amount). The pan-Canadian PEPPOL e-invoicing framework is voluntary for B2B/B2G transactions. Non-resident simplified GST/HST registrants file periodic returns via CRA GST/HST NETFILE and retain supporting records for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: SaaS subscriptions (intangible personal property) supplied to a non-resident person who is not a GST/HST registrant are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI s.10 if the supply is not in respect of real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada. Supply of the software right to merchant-of-record platforms (Paddle/Lemon Squeezy) located outside Canada generally qualifies for zero-rating; the MoR collects and remits Canadian GST/HST on end-consumer sales. Goods exported qualify for zero-rating under Schedule VI Part V. SaaS supplied to Canadian consumers is taxable at 5% GST (or applicable HST/provincial QST/PST depending on place of supply).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export records for goods
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical export of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank FX credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds

For digital services/SaaS: order-to-cash records showing non-resident status of recipient — IP-address geolocation logs, billing address, executed SaaS agreement, payment-provider records (Paddle/Lemon Squeezy dashboard reports), and evidence the recipient is not GST/HST-registered
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal 4-year period (extended to 7 years for misrepresentation or neglect). Misapplied zero-rating triggers reassessment for uncollected 5% GST/HST, prescribed daily compound interest, and arrears penalties. ETA s.285(1) false-statement penalty equals the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax sought to be evaded; ETA s.222(1) makes a supplier liable for tax it failed to collect. Serious fraudulent export claims may lead to criminal prosecution under ETA s.327 — fines up to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years on indictment — plus retrospective clawback of refunds and input tax credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (head office in Ottawa) acts as the central monetary authority for the Canadian dollar. Foreign-exchange policy and administration are shared with the Department of Finance Canada under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. Prudential supervision of banks is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and cross-border AML/CFT reporting obligations are supervised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (CBCA) — including Individuals with Significant Control declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution by the Director; reinstatement requires court order, payment of all arrears, and filing compliance. No late fee is imposed for a single missed annual return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return with Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end due June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat failure attracts an additional penalty per infraction; daily compound interest applies; willful non-filing may be prosecuted criminally.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No CBCA size threshold for non-distributing private corporations; every CBCA corporation must appoint an auditor at its first annual meeting unless all shareholders unanimously waive the appointment (non-distributing corporations only). Distributing corporations and those required by shareholders or securities regulators must have a mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private enterprises may elect IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA requires every corporation to maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC). Changes in ISC must be recorded within 15 days; the annual return must indicate whether there are ISCs and include prescribed ISC information if none has been filed. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation filing. Share transfers must be recorded promptly in the Register of Members and, if applicable, the ISC register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$100–US$400 per year for Canadian registered agent/office services; include provincial registered office address fees where applicable.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000–US$12,000 for a small SaaS corporation if audit cannot be waived; typical non-audit review or compilation is lower.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal Part I general corporate income tax rate (fully taxable CCPC); reduced to 9% federal small business rate on active business income up to the shared federal small business limit of C$500,000; provincial/territorial corporate tax applies separately (e.g., 8%–16%, varying by province of permanent establishment)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate on first C$500,000 active business income); SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable for CCPCs up to C$3M qualifying expenditures); 10% federal abatement on provincial-apportioned income; general tax rate reduction to 13.5% for non-SBD eligible income; 100% immediate CCA for eligible computer hardware? No—software acquired after certain dates? Actually, for SaaS, Canadian software should be deducted via CCA Class 12 (100%) or Class 8 (20% declining). Let me be precise: Computer application software — Class 12 at 100% (if acquired and available for use before... or if it's
